main_text.p: Huius horrendi simul, & singularis exem-plo memorandi casus historiam, sui-mo artificio, ab artifice summo depi&am, potius quàm descriptam, a- verò non infeliciter, fortasse, Gallic-is senariis rithmis expressam, subiice-re hic libuit, eo quem in illo tetrastich-o notaui fructu, amatoribus legendam at-que meditandam.
main_text.head: CÆDES DIDONIS ἀντέχεπος Virgilio descripta, Æneid. lib. iv.

p.i: AT trepida & cœptis immanibus effera Dido,

l.i: Dardanium, non hoc quaesitum munus in usus.
Hic postquam Iliacas vestes, notumque cubile
Consp exit, paulum lacrymis & mente morata,
Dulces exuviae, dum fata deusque sinebant,
Accipite hanc animam, meque his exsoluite curis,
Vixi, & quem dederat cursum fortuna peregi,
Et nunc magna mei sub terras ibit imago.
Vrbem praeclaram statui, mea moenia vidi:

page.notes: Left edge and right edge are cut off by the scan; the first line of the verse is partly lost at the right. Several words are damaged and read with doubt, notably "Consp exit" (Conspexit), "Dulces exuviae" line, and the Greek heading word. The printed text of the tetrastich and the Greek heading may not be fully legible.
